correctness.rationale: The finite iid rates define a continuous nondecreasing operational clock A_t, independent of the unit-rate symmetric walk. Conditional time change is valid including zero-rate intervals. Reflection gives survival at operational time a from x as the sum of the unrestricted kernel at displacements 1−x through x. This is between h_1(a) and 2x h_1(a), since every term is at most the mass at 0. Monotonicity sandwiches the mean between the positive-epoch and zero-included epoch sums times τ. At epochs the clock has transform φ(τs)^m; the h_1 Fourier kernel 1+cos θ is nonnegative so Tonelli sums it to the resolvent even in the divergent case. Only θ=0 is singular, since P(R>0)>0; s=τ(1−cos θ) gives a Jacobian comparable to s^(−1/2) near zero. Karamata yields the asserted Laplace deficit for 0<α<1, Potter bounds separate the strict power cases, and u=1/s gives the critical integral and the strict cutoff κ>1. The proposed critical tails are continuous, decreasing above their cutoff and tend to zero. No positive or finite moment is used. The finite checker was inspected, not executed, and cannot establish convergence at the critical endpoint.
